intro: How many buttons fit in a jar? How many cups of lemonade can you sell in a weekend? Big numbers are everywhere. This unit shows you how big numbers are built. Every number up to 1,000 is made of hundreds, tens and ones.

You will read and write numbers to 1,000. You will compare them with >, < and =. You will count by 5s, 10s and 100s. Then you will add and subtract big numbers by trading tens and ones. And you will explain why your way works.
bigQuestion: How do hundreds, tens and ones let us count, compare, add and subtract numbers up to 1,000?

timeline.t: Count buttons one by one and lose your place
Make groups of ten so counting goes faster
Ten groups of ten make one hundred
Ten hundreds fill the jar: one thousand
Write a number as hundreds, tens and ones
Add cups sold: tens with tens, ones with ones
Trade ten ones for a ten when there are too many
Trade a ten for ten ones so you can subtract
Add and subtract hundreds with drawings
Explain your strategy and check it another way

words.d: a group of ten tens, or 100 ones
a number written as hundreds plus tens plus ones, like 300 + 40 + 7
to count by jumps of the same size, like 5, 10, 15, 20
a number that makes pairs with none left over, like 2, 4, 6
to trade ten ones for one ten, or one ten for ten ones
the answer you get when you add
the answer you get when you subtract

test.q: What number is 6 hundreds, 0 tens and 4 ones?

test.why: 2 hundreds is 200. 7 tens is 70. 5 ones is 5. So 200 + 70 + 5.
The hundreds tie. 4 tens is less than 8 tens. So 348 < 384.
56 ends in 6. It makes 28 pairs with none left over. 56 is even.
655 + 100 = 755. The hundreds digit goes from 6 to 7.
6 + 7 = 13. Trade ten ones for a ten. 2 + 4 + 1 = 7 tens. So 73.
Trade: 8 tens and 11 ones. 11 − 5 = 6. 8 − 3 = 5 tens. So 56.

write.prompt: Solve 53 − 27. Show each step with tens and ones. Explain why you traded a ten. Then check your answer by adding.
tips: Show the trade: 4 tens and 13 ones.
Say why: 3 ones is not enough to take away 7.
